fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. The verse says Caleb "…drove out from there the three sons of Anak…" the descendants of Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. Three of them, and Caleb drove them out. I can't even drive the crumbs off my counter, and they're not even big (Joshua 15:14).

Hmm, not quite, friend. The text never mentions Caleb paying anybody. It says he "…drove out from there the three sons of Anak…" Driving them out is what the verse gives us, and that's the answer here (Joshua 15:14).

Good guess, baker, but a treaty isn't in this verse. The text never mentions one. It says Caleb "…drove out from there the three sons of Anak…" Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai's descendants (Joshua 15:14).

Fair guess, baker, but the verse has Caleb asking something else. When she gets off her donkey, he asks, "What do you desire?" His question is about what she wants, not how long anybody is staying (Joshua 15:18).
True, baker! Acsah asks for springs, and the verse says "…Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs." Two springs, upper and lower. I love that for her (Joshua 15:19).

Correct, baker. The text says "…the descendants of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem." It's a little hard to read after all those cities, but it's honest. The verse says that to this day the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah (Joshua 15:63).

That would be a tidy ending, friend, but it's not in the text. The verse says Judah "…could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem." It also says the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah, so they stay (Joshua 15:63).
